title: Console scope rebalance: prioritize per-route cost quickcards and lightweight trace sampler
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Context: Our original Console launch scope included a full per-route analytics dashboard, deep trace visualization, and a detailed cost-breakdown table. With limited eng bandwidth and telemetry storage cost concerns, we are rebalancing to land a compact, high-impact surface that gives product teams actionable signal while deferring heavier investments. This ticket captures the scope cuts, acceptance criteria, and rollout constraints for the trimmed deliverable: two 'quickcards' (per-route RPS/median latency and per-route token cost estimate) plus a lightweight trace sampling UI that links to full traces in observability backends.
decision_record: Decisions made on 2025-02-19: 1) Cut: defer the full per-route time-series heatmap and long-tail percentile explorer to H2. 2) Keep: quickcards for cost and latency because they enable immediate cost optimization. 3) Replace: heavy trace viewer with a compact sampled-trace list + direct deep-link into existing tracing backend (e.g., Tempo) to avoid building an in-house trace renderer. 4) Telemetry: reduce retention for Console-specific spans to 7d to control cost; provide opt-in extended retention behind a paid toggle. Rationale: prioritize developer value (cost visibility + quick root-cause) while reducing front-end and backend implementation scope by ~40%.

acceptance_criteria:
1) Quickcard: Per-route latency card shows median latency and 95th percentile with last-1h / last-24h toggle; values match backend metrics to within 5%.
2) Quickcard: Per-route cost card displays estimated cost per 1k requests and a monthlyized estimate for the selected window; cost computation is documented and reproducible (link to pricing formula).
3) Trace sampler UI: Presents sampled traces for a selected route with timestamp, span count, and a direct deep-link to the full trace in tracing backend. Clicking opens the external trace viewer in a new tab.
4) Frontend uses existing Console layout components; no new global state stores introduced.
5) Telemetry retention for Console spans set to 7 days by default; customer-facing notice added to Console settings explaining tradeoff and opt-in for extended retention.
6) End-to-end tests: smoke tests validate quickcard rendering, sample list pagination, and deep-link format.
7) Performance: quickcards load under 800ms for typical routes in staging environment.
8) Observability: dashboard tile created in internal Grafana showing API errors and latency for the new endpoints; SLO owners notified.
9) Documentation: PRD updated, user-facing help doc created, and Console release notes drafted.
implementation_notes: Backend: ENG-84321 must provide per-route token meters and an aggregated cost feed for the last-1h/24h window. Use existing metrics exporter; implement a lightweight aggregation lambda to avoid touching core runtime. Frontend: reuse OverviewCard component; Quickcards should be lazy-loaded and server-render friendly. Tracing: use sampling service to tag sample metadata and provide external deep-link URL template; do not store full traces in Console. Avoid new read-models that increase telemetry ingestion volume.
qa_notes: Create a test tenant with synthetic traffic to validate cost estimates. Confirm edge cases: routes with very low RPS (<0.1 rps), routes with bursty traffic, and routes mapped to dedicated capacity. Validate that the opt-in extended retention correctly toggles downstream retention policies. Include manual test for deep-link navigation into Tempo and for account access permissions.
rollout_plan: Canary rollout to 10% of orgs for 48 hours with feature flag. Monitor error rate and page load time; rollback if quickcard API latency >1s or error rate increases by >2x baseline. After 48h, ramp to 100% over 72h if metrics stable. Inform customer success of the change and add a short walkthrough for early adopters.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Cost estimates may be misunderstood by customers; mitigation: show calculation tooltip and link to billing docs. Risk: Sampling misses a critical trace during incident; mitigation: allow ad-hoc trace export in the deep-link and keep sampling rate adjustable per-tenant. Risk: Telemetry retention reduction triggers compliance concerns; mitigation: provide paid opt-in and alert legal/compliance teams before launch.
